Beam-search chain Fast-and-Frugal Tree

Source: R/beam.R
run_beam_fft.Rd

Searches the chain-FFT space (depth `max_levels`, one cue per node, binary exits) by beam search over all (cue, direction, threshold, exit-pattern) combinations. The search optimizes balanced accuracy on the training set; output is a chain of depth at most `max_levels`.

Usage

run_beam_fft(
  train,
  test,
  max_levels = 4L,
  beam_B = 10L,
  max_thresholds_per_cue = 5L,
  item_cap = 50
)

Arguments

train, test

`data.table`s with binary criterion in column `y`.

max_levels

Maximum chain depth (1-4).

beam_B

Beam width — number of partial chains carried forward between depth levels.

max_thresholds_per_cue

For each numeric cue, the top `K` midpoint thresholds by marginal normalized MI are kept.

item_cap

Maximum number of (cue, direction, threshold) items retained for the search; pre-ranked by marginal balanced accuracy. `Inf` keeps all.

Value

List with the standard runner contract: * `pred` — integer vector of test predictions (0/1) * `n_cues_per_row` — integer vector of exit levels (1..d) * `train_time` — elapsed seconds * `chain_def` — `data.table` with columns `level, cue, direction, threshold, exit` * `notes` — diagnostic string

Details

Hyperparameter defaults `max_levels = 4`, `beam_B = 10`, `max_thresholds_per_cue = 5`, `item_cap = 50` correspond to the D-optimal-DoE-selected configuration ("beam-doe09") used in the accompanying paper.

See also

[adaptive_fft()] races this against FFTrees `ifan` on an inner holdout.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
  d <- load_fft_dataset("heartdisease")
  in_tr <- make_split(d$y, seed = 42)
  r <- run_beam_fft(d[in_tr], d[!in_tr])
  m_bacc(d$y[!in_tr], r$pred)
} # }
